Class StringCodec

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.transform.text.StringCodec
All Implemented Interfaces:
Codec<String>
public final class StringCodec extends Object implements Codec<String>
A Codec<String> whose bytes are simply the text in a charset — no quoting, no framing. This is what a backend's create(String.class) does not give you: a JSON backend encodes hello as the seven bytes "hello". Use this for payloads that already are text, and as a backend-free base for Codec.xmap(Function, Function): 
Codec<UUID> ids = StringCodec.utf8().xmap(UUID::fromString, UUID::toString);

Decoding is strict: bytes that are not valid in the charset are rejected with InvalidPayloadException rather than silently replaced with U+FFFD, so corruption surfaces as an error instead of a wrong answer. Encoding uses the JDK's default replacement for characters the charset cannot represent (an unpaired surrogate in UTF-8, a non-Latin character in ISO-8859-1 becomes ?).

Instances are immutable and thread-safe.
